{"rules": ["Model consistently overestimates the 30-day average when recent history shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., >84 EUR) followed by high volatility.", "Forecast bias increases significantly after a positive sentiment signal (0.50) appears in the last 2 days of history, causing an overshoot of ~1.5-2.0 EUR compared to true outcomes.", "True outcomes exhibit strong mean reversion and downward pressure within the first 10 days of the forecast horizon, whereas models predict a steady linear increase.", "When sentiment remains near zero (0.00) for >10 consecutive days prior to forecasting, the model's upward drift is invalid; actual prices tend to flatten or decline rather than rise.", "The model fails to capture the 'volatility compression' effect where high recent prices are followed by a rapid drop in the forecast horizon, leading to systematic over-forecasting of the 30-day mean."]
